tagline: Gravel rangeland, then the river gorge.
intro: From US 20, Highway 27 runs north through open range and private ranches, with basalt buttes above the rolling country. The first eighteen miles are gravel. Beyond the start of pavement, the road crosses Bowman Dam’s spillway and drops into the Crooked River gorge.

Campgrounds follow the river toward Prineville, and Chimney Rock rises above the highway. In town, the old Crook County Bank keeps its bronze teller cages inside a museum named for the same Arthur Bowman as the dam.

moments.title: Bowman Dam
moments.text: The road crosses the spillway of the dam holding Prineville Reservoir, then descends into the river gorge.

moments.title: Chimney Rock
moments.text: Across the highway from Chimney Rock Campground, a trail climbs 1.3 miles to the butte above the road.

moments.title: Bowman Museum
moments.text: The old bank’s bronze teller cages and marble counters share their rooms with exhibits on Crook County’s history.

practical: The southernmost eighteen miles are graded gravel suitable for passenger vehicles; much of the route is open range, with limited or absent cell service.
